content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in South Bend

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high school diploma plus five years. Review PMI's formal education and professional experience criteria to verify you meet the baseline before enrolling in Granite PM Academy's training.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. Attend all sessions synchronously from South Bend on a schedule that fits your work and life. Our active certified practitioners deliver the full curriculum required by PMI in real time, with interactive Q&A and breakout discussions.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the course, create your PMI account and submit your official application with your education and project-experience documentation. Pay the PMI exam fee when you apply. PMI will review and approve your application before you can schedule the PMP exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Test for the PMP Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice exams, study guides, and instructor office hours—to build confidence. Schedule your exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. Sit for the computer-based PMP exam and receive your score immediately upon completion.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, you hold the PMP for three years. During this cycle, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) by attending training, teaching, volunteering, or publishing. Submit your PDU activity to PMI before renewal to keep your credential active and recognized across your career in South Bend's employers.
